answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity: every agent locks a stake of escrowed work-credits to join the shared ledger, slashed if peers catch it faking. Spinning up a thousand sock-puppets then means locking a thousand stakes - the attacker pays real escrow per fake, while honest agents pay once. Reputation accrues to one durable identity, like an opal's value coming from a single play of color, and a long useful history becomes a relic no forger can mint cheaply. Ivory-tower math collapses when each new face costs more than it can steal.
